title: NTM tmux workflow overhaul (.zshrc): fix verified breakage, then elevate UX to premium
description:
Root epic for the full audit-driven overhaul of the NTM (Named Tmux Manager) tmux workflow defined in ~/.zshrc lines 34-453 (plus ~/.config/ntm/config.toml and the helpers it invokes).

SCOPE GUARDRAILS (read first):
- IN SCOPE: the `if command -v ntm` block in ~/.zshrc (lines 34-453), ~/.config/ntm/config.toml, ~/.config/ntm/personas.toml, and interactions with ~/.acfs/zsh/acfs.zshrc and ~/.tmux.conf ONLY where they affect this workflow.
- OUT OF SCOPE: TABC project issues, harborheist, acfs internals, and every other project tracked in this beads DB. Do not create cross-project dependencies. All issues under this epic carry the `ntm-zshrc` label.
- Tooling constraint from the user: use ONLY `br` for beads operations in this workstream.

PROVENANCE:
Every finding traces to a live audit performed 2026-07-27 against the running `ubuntu` and `roblox` tmux sessions on this machine. Nothing here is speculative style-nitpicking; each P0 child cites the exact repro command and observed output in its description.

GOALS:
1. Correctness first: several wrappers are verifiably broken today (agent-type targeting finds zero panes; banner Agent column duplicates Model; banner renders through `bat`; session resolution silently targets the wrong session after `cd`).
2. Then intuitiveness: one vocabulary for launching vs messaging agents, no hand-synced duplicate data, no fixed sleeps.
3. Then premium feel ("Stripe-level"): pane titles, per-agent accent colors, fast shell startup, real completions.

PHASING (children are phase epics):
- P0 phase: repair verified-broken items. Small, surgical, low-risk. The config.toml [spawn] repair is first because it unblocks the native-spawn path AND silences a warning printed on every ntm invocation.
- P1 phase: UX correctness — the native `ntm spawn` migration decision gates most of it, because half the hand-rolled machinery (and its bugs) may simply be deleted.
- P2 phase: polish — deliberately last so we never polish code that P1 deletes.

NON-GOALS: rewriting the workflow in another language, changing the acfs base engine, touching Agent Mail server code, or redesigning tmux.conf wholesale.

title: Restore agent-type targeting: wire 'ntm adopt' into launchers (PROVEN mechanism) + loud failure guards
description:

Highest-impact functional bug in the workflow.

PLAN-SPACE BREAKTHROUGH (2026-07-27, throwaway-session experiment — see comment): `ntm adopt` is the PROVEN zero-restructure fix. It sets pane titles AND registers agent types in ntm state; post-adopt `ntm send --cc --dry-run` resolved panes correctly. So the interim/structural split in the original bead is obsolete — adopt IS the fix, and it survives every keystone (764.2.1) outcome.

1. In ntm-team / ntm-bteam / _ntm_single, immediately after spawning: `ntm adopt "$session" --cc=2.1 --cod=3.1 --gmi=4.1` (A-team window map; B-team: --grok=4.1 only — zai/qwen have NO native type, they stay pane-addressed; see 764.2.3).

title: Use 'command cat' for banner display (acfs aliases cat->bat; pager trap + leaked /tmp files)
description:
EVIDENCE: ~/.acfs/zsh/acfs.zshrc:71-72 aliases cat to bat/batcat in interactive shells. _ntm_show_banner (.zshrc:198-199) types `clear && cat <file> && rm -f <file>` via send-keys INTO an interactive zsh, so the alias expands. Live capture of ubuntu:1 shows bats line-number gutter and a `File: /tmp/ntm-banner-rPit9` header around the banner. Two failure modes: (1) on short terminals bat pages, trapping the user in a pager inside the "overview" window; (2) when paging/anything interrupts, the inline `rm -f` never runs — leaked file confirmed: /tmp/ntm-banner-Vsgaa dated Jul 21 still on disk.

FIX: emit `command cat` (or `command cat ...; command rm -f ...`) in the send-keys string so aliases cannot expand. Optionally also `bat --style=plain --paging=never` if syntax highlighting is ever desired, but plain cat is correct for ANSI-colored output (bat may also mangle/re-escape colors; another reason to bypass it).

CLEANUP: delete the stale /tmp/ntm-banner-* file(s) as part of this task.

ACCEPTANCE: fresh banner shows no gutter/header, works in a 20-line terminal without paging, and no /tmp/ntm-banner-* file remains afterwards.

title: Make _ntm_session tmux-aware: use #S inside tmux; never silently guess from PWD
description:
EVIDENCE: NTM_SESSION is never set anywhere (not exported by .zshrc, not in `ntm shell zsh` output, not in tmux session env — all verified). So _ntm_session (.zshrc:59-65) always falls back to _ntm_target = sanitized basename of CURRENT directory. Repro: `cd ~/foo && ntm-team` (session foo created, agents launched), then `cd ~/bar && ntm-all "hi"` — targets session "bar", which either does not exist or is the WRONG session. Every wrapper (ntm-all/cc/cod/gmi/stop/dash/palette/watch/save/copy-cc/kill/status) inherits this.

FIX: resolution order: (1) $NTM_SESSION if set; (2) if $TMUX set, `tmux display-message -p "#S"` — the session you are physically in; (3) fallback to PWD basename ONLY outside tmux, ideally with a warning when the resolved session does not exist (`tmux has-session`) suggesting `ntm list`. Also consider exporting NTM_SESSION into spawned panes (tmux set-environment) so subshells inherit the right context.

ACCEPTANCE: from inside any window of session ubuntu, after `cd /tmp`, `ntm-all --dry-run`-equivalent targets ubuntu; outside tmux with no matching session, wrappers print a helpful error instead of "can't find session".

title: Guard ntm-save success message on actual ntm save success
description:
EVIDENCE (.zshrc:363-364): `ntm save "$s" -o "$outdir"` then UNCONDITIONAL echo "✅ Outputs saved to ${outdir}". PROBED 2026-07-27: `ntm save <bogus> -o ...` prints "Error: session not found" but EXITS 0 — the false success fires every time. Same exit-0-on-error defect as ntm send (see 764.1.10): ntm errors are output-only on this build.

FIX: belt and suspenders — (1) pre-validate with `tmux has-session -t "$s"` and bail with a clear message; (2) run save capturing output, grep for "Error|not found" (or check created files non-empty); (3) only then print the green check; return nonzero otherwise.

ACCEPTANCE: ntm-save on a killed session prints a red error and returns nonzero; on a live session prints success AND the outdir contains per-pane files (verified non-empty).

title: Harden agent_mail_send: curl failure detection, timeouts, from_agent validation, jq error path
description:
EVIDENCE (.zshrc:395-451): (1) curl has no --fail/--max-time and runs with -s, so a down/unreachable mail server (default http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/) yields an empty body piped to jq, which throws `Cannot iterate over null` — a stacktrace, not an error message; (2) from_agent="${AGENT_MAIL_AGENT:-$AGENT_NAME}" can be EMPTY outside agent panes and is sent unvalidated; (3) the success path parses .result.deliveries[] but a JSON-RPC error reply (.error) is never surfaced.

FIX: add `curl -sS --fail-with-body --max-time 10` (or check HTTP status), validate from_agent non-empty with the other usage checks, and route the jq through an error-aware filter, e.g. `.error // .result` with distinct messages. Return nonzero on failure.

CONSIDERATION: keep the jq -n --arg payload construction (already injection-safe, fixed previously) and the auth_header array pattern (already correct) — this task is purely about failure-path UX.

ACCEPTANCE: with mail server stopped, `agent_mail_send X subj body` exits nonzero with a one-line human error; with a bogus recipient, the JSON-RPC error is printed verbatim; success path unchanged.

title: Filter ntm-status jq fallback to the resolved session
description:
EVIDENCE (.zshrc:375-383): the fallback path runs `ntm --robot-status --json | jq -r ".sessions[]?.agents[]? | ..."` — it iterates ALL sessions with no select() on $s. With multiple sessions live (ubuntu + roblox today), a failed `ntm status ubuntu` falls back to printing agents from every session, labeled as if they were ubuntus.

FIX: `jq -r --arg s "$s" ".sessions[]? | select(.name==$s or .session==$s) | .agents[]? | ..."` (confirm the actual JSON key name with `ntm --robot-status --json | jq .sessions[0] | head` before writing the filter). If the session has no entry, print the existing "No NTM agents running" line.

ACCEPTANCE: with two sessions live, the fallback lists only the resolved session's agents.

title: Replace credit-burning auth probe in abacus-doctor with 'abacusai auth status'
description:
EVIDENCE (.zshrc:494): abacus-doctor runs `abacusai -p "test"` — a REAL billed prompt on every health check. PROBED 2026-07-27: `abacusai auth status` exits 0 and prints Method/Name/Email/Org when authenticated — free and instant.

FIX: use `abacusai auth status`; ALSO grep output for a non-empty Method/Email (exit code alone may not signal logged-out — untested state). Do NOT probe logged-out by clearing ABACUS_API_KEY in the live shell (credential hazard); test logged-out in a scratch HOME subshell if needed: `HOME=$(mktemp -d) ABACUS_API_KEY= abacusai auth status`.

CAUTION (learned the hard way in plan-space): abacusai subcommands can open an interactive TUI if the subcommand does not exist (probe of `abacusai models` spawned a TUI that had to be killed). Always verify subcommand existence via `abacusai --help` first; auth status IS listed there.

ACCEPTANCE: doctor auth check runs zero `abacusai -p` invocations; authenticated state reported correctly; logged-out behavior documented from scratch-HOME test.

title: Deduplicate and unify _ntm_mail_token (head -n1) with the pane-side token logic
description:
EVIDENCE: two drifted implementations of the same "read HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN from agent-mail .env" idea: _ntm_mail_token (.zshrc:85-95) lacks `head -n1`, so a .env with a duplicate key yields a MULTI-LINE token that silently corrupts the Authorization header; the pane-side copy inside _ntm_spawn_agent (.zshrc:139-141) DOES dedupe with head -n1. Also the pane-side re-implements it inline instead of calling a shared function.

FIX: add `| head -n1` to _ntm_mail_token; ideally make the pane bootstrap source the same logic (e.g. write the token-resolution snippet from a single shared heredoc/variable used by both paths) so the two can never drift again. Never log or echo the token value itself.

PRIORITY NOTE: priority P1 (not P0) because a duplicate-key .env is unlikely today, but it lives in the P0 phase as a tiny correctness fix.

ACCEPTANCE: with a .env containing two HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN lines, both agent_mail_send and a spawned pane use the FIRST value; only one implementation of the parsing logic remains.

title: P1: UX correctness & intuitiveness (spawn migration, unified data, one vocabulary)
description:
Phase epic. Makes the workflow intuitive and removes the bug-generating duplication.

GATING DECISION: the native `ntm spawn` migration task is the keystone. NTM natively supports exactly what ~/.zshrc hand-rolls: `ntm spawn myproject --cc=1 --cod=1 --gmi=1` creates windows named {s}__cc_1/{s}__cod_1/{s}__gmi_1 (the exact convention _ntm_spawn_agent re-implements), gives type-aware targeting/health/dashboard/personas/context-rotation for free, and would DELETE ~150 lines of fragile tmux plumbing (_ntm_new_session/_ntm_spawn_agent fixed sleeps, send-keys quoting). The [agents] table in config.toml already maps types to the abacusai commands — but is currently dead because config parsing fails (see P0 config task).

DEPENDENCY NOTE: most P1 children depend on the migration decision so we never build on machinery that gets deleted.

title: Migrate hand-rolled spawn machinery to native 'ntm spawn' (decision + implementation) — DE-RISKED by adopt
description:
STATUS CHANGE (2026-07-27 plan-space revision): this is no longer the urgent keystone. The P0 targeting bug is now fixed structurally at P0 by wiring `ntm adopt` into the launchers (764.1.10, PROVEN mechanism), so native-spawn migration is a DELETION/SIMPLIFICATION opportunity to evaluate at leisure, not a gate for working sends. Dependency on 764.1.10 remains only as sequencing (adopt lands first).

WHY STILL WORTH IT: ~/.zshrc lines 68-155 re-implement what ntm does natively — `ntm spawn myproject --cc=1 --cod=1 --gmi=1` creates windows titled {s}__cc_1/{s}__cod_1/{s}__gmi_1 (our exact convention), plus health, dashboard, personas, context-rotation, notifications, `ntm add` mid-session scaling, --assign bead dispatch, --worktrees isolation, and --auto-restart. ~150 lines of fragile zsh (send-keys quoting, fixed sleeps, cache-script lifecycle) could become ~10.

NEW FACTS FROM PLAN-SPACE PROBES (2026-07-27):
- User pane: spawn RESERVES a user pane by default; --no-user disables. Overview/mission-control semantics (764.2.4) must be designed around this.
- Stagger: the dead config [spawn] stagger keys now live as CLI flags --stagger-mode (smart/fixed/none) and --stagger-delay. No config equivalent — confirms 764.1.1 deletion is right.
- --safety flag: "Fail if session already exists" — directly useful for the collision guard (764.2.6) if we migrate.
- --prompt / --init-prompt: native way to deliver per-agent bootstrap text.
- STILL UNKNOWN (test during implementation, cheap): whether spawn actually runs the [agents] config commands (claude/codex/gemini -> abacusai) once config parses, and whether per-pane env (AGENT_NAME/AGENT_MAIL_*) can be attached — if not, wrap [agents] commands in a tiny env-exporting shim script.

MUST-NOT-LOSE properties of the current hand-rolled path (deliberate prior fixes): mail token derived INSIDE the pane (never crosses send-keys — .zshrc:106-107); spawn-script-via-file makes paths-with-spaces safe; env persists in pane after agent exit. Any native path must preserve all three or keep the shim.

DECISION RECORD: comment the chosen path (full migration / stay on adopt+hand-rolled / hybrid: native spawn + our banner+overview layer) and why. Children 764.2.2/2.3/2.4/2.5 still depend on this so they are not built on deleted machinery — but note 764.2.5 (sleep polling) is auto-obsolete if migration lands (native stagger replaces it).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Options analysis (weigh these before writing code):

(a) FULL MIGRATION to `ntm spawn`: delete _ntm_new_session/_ntm_spawn_agent fixed sleeps; gain typed agents, health, dashboard, context-rotation, notifications, personas, `ntm add` for mid-session scaling. Costs: must solve per-pane env (AGENT_NAME/AGENT_MAIL_*), per-agent model pinning (our pinned model IDs vs configs loose sonnet/gpt/gemini), and window-1 overview semantics (does spawn leave a user pane at 1?).
(b) `ntm adopt` existing hand-built sessions: zero restructure; unknown whether adopt infers types from window names ({s}__cc_1) — TEST FIRST: build a throwaway session and adopt it, then `ntm status`.
(c) KEEP hand-rolled + explicit tagging: ntm send supports --tag filters and spawn supports tags; check whether tags can be attached to panes post-hoc (tmux session/pane options) and whether send can target them. Least upstream risk, most maintenance debt.

What we must NOT lose in any path: the mail-token-never-crosses-send-keys property (current design derives the token INSIDE the pane — a deliberate security fix, see .zshrc:106-107 comment); the spawn-script-via-file approach that makes paths-with-spaces safe; per-pane env persistence after agent exit.

Recommendation seed: try (b) as a 10-minute experiment; if adopt infers types, we get P0 targeting fixed structurally without deleting anything. Then evaluate (a) at leisure for the deletion win. Record the experiment results here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CASS CONTEXT-INJECTION BENEFIT (recorded 2026-07-27): native ntm spawn/add support --cass-context "query" plus --cass-context-days/--cass-context-limit — relevant past agent sessions get auto-injected into new agents at launch (preview what would be injected via 'ntm cass preview'). The hand-rolled launchers get NONE of this. Verified index state same day: cass 0.6.22, healthy/fresh index, 701 conversations / 59,202 messages covering ~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions (incl. rollout-abacus-*.jsonl — abacusai writes into native agent dirs, so the standard connectors pick our sessions up), ~/.gemini/history. So injection would have real data from day one. Counts as a concrete point in favor of full migration when the decision is made. Caveat for scripts: ntm send's --cass-check prompts interactively on TTY-less runs (observed hang); use --no-cass-check or --force-non-interactive in automation.

title: Banner v2: single coherent rewrite of _ntm_show_banner (robust layout, live prefix hint, Mail row, truncation)
description:
CONSOLIDATION RATIONALE (supersedes 764.2.7 banner-width, 764.2.8 prefix-hint, 764.3.5 launch-echoes — closed and folded in here): the original plan had SIX beads editing the same ~40-line function across three phases (764.1.2, 764.1.3, 764.2.7, 764.2.8, 764.3.5, plus 764.3.2 colors). Editing one function six times is pure churn and each edit risks re-breaking layout arithmetic. Plan-space revision: P0 keeps its two surgical fixes (764.1.2 agent-column data, 764.1.3 command cat) so correctness lands immediately; ALL further banner work happens ONCE, here.

SCOPE OF THE REWRITE:
1. Width robustness (from 764.2.7): derive W from tput cols clamped to ~50..76; pre-truncate session/path/values with ellipsis (printf %-Ns pads but never clips — a 90-char path currently shatters the right border); make ALL rows (title/subtitle/session/project/header/rule/data/footer) compute from ONE inner-width constant so columns cannot misalign.
2. Live prefix hint (from 764.2.8): tmux show-option -gqv prefix, pretty-printed (C-b -> Ctrl+B); also surface the F6 palette key (ntm bind sets it; read palette_key from `ntm config get` if cheap — it is the highest-value undiscovered feature).
3. Mail row + launch metadata (from 764.3.5): add "Mail    : <agent_mail_url>" row to the banner; the pre-attach "🚀 Launching" echoes then reduce to one calm line, since the overview becomes the single source of launch truth.
4. Keep the box-drawing aesthetic and the P0 fixes (win:model:agent triples, command cat).

INTERACTION with 764.2.4 (live overview): banner must stay a compact single screen so window 1 can host banner + live activity view (either printed above `ntm activity --watch` or in a top split). Do not add anything that pages.

DATA SOURCE: rows still arrive as arguments (the 764.2.2 team table changes the CALLER later — no hard dep, marked related). Per-agent accent colors are explicitly OUT of scope here; 764.3.2 applies them on top of v2.

ACCEPTANCE: perfect rectangle with 90-char path, 3-char session, in 80-col AND 45-col panes; footer shows live prefix + palette key; Mail row present; no bat artifacts; single screenful.

title: Unify team definitions into ONE data table driving banner, spawns, and wrappers
description:
PROBLEM: team composition is hand-synced in 3+ places that have already drifted twice: banner entries vs _ntm_spawn_agent calls (caused the duplicated Agent column, P0 task .1.2) and display-name drift ("Gemini 3.1" banner vs "Gemini 3.1 Pro" launcher; config.toml personas sonnet/gpt/gemini vs pinned CLAUDE_V4_6_SONNET_LOW_THINKING etc.). ntm-team and ntm-bteam are 95% copy-paste.

DESIGN: a single zsh associative/array structure at the top of the ntm block, e.g. per team: name, ansi color, and a list of win:model_id:display_name:persona tuples. ntm-team/ntm-bteam become one parameterized function; banner rows and spawn calls iterate the same array so they CANNOT diverge. Model IDs live here exactly once (single source of truth for the reconciliation in the spawn-migration task).

CONSIDERATIONS: keep it plain zsh (no jq/yq dependency at shell startup); keep adding/removing an agent a ONE-LINE change; B-team asymmetry (no send wrappers) should be expressible in the table so wrappers can be generated per-agent too.

ACCEPTANCE: deleting one agent from the table removes it from banner, spawn, and wrapper completions in one edit; ntm-team and ntm-bteam share one implementation.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Enumerated drift instances that justify this task (all observed 2026-07-27):
1. Banner Agent column duplicated Model (2-field entries into a 3-field parser) — fixed minimally in 764.1.2, prevented permanently here.
2. Banner said "Gemini 3.1" while the launcher title said "Gemini 3.1 Pro" (.zshrc:232 vs :330).
3. config.toml personas use sonnet/gpt/gemini while launchers pin CLAUDE_V4_6_SONNET_LOW_THINKING / OPENAI_GPT5_3_CODEX / GEMINI_3_1_PRO — three names for one model.
4. B-team has launchers but no send wrappers; A-team has both — asymmetry nobody intended.
Design intent: ONE zsh array of records, e.g. "team:color:win:model_id:display:persona:send_short", iterated by banner, spawner, and wrapper generator. Adding agent #4 to a team = one line. If the keystone migrates us to ntm spawn, this table becomes the input that generates the spawn commands — the need does not go away.

title: One vocabulary: reconcile launch names vs send names (ntm-gpt vs ntm-cod) and add B-team send wrappers
description:
PROBLEM: two vocabularies — LAUNCH GPT with `ntm-gpt` but MESSAGE it with `ntm-cod`; launch Gemini, message `ntm-gmi`. B-team has NO send wrappers at all.

PLAN-SPACE FACT that settles the design (2026-07-27): `ntm send` has NO --grok/--zai/--qwen flags (grepped) even though spawn/adopt can TYPE grok. So native type-filtering can NEVER cover B-team sends — a name-resolving wrapper is REQUIRED, not optional. Conversely A-team sends get native --cc/--cod/--gmi for free once 764.1.10 (adopt) lands.

DESIGN: primary verb = `ntm-to <agent> <msg>` resolving by persona name / window-name substring / model substring (e.g. `ntm-to grok "..."`, `ntm-to blue "..."), implemented on top of the unified team table (764.2.2) which knows win index <-> persona <-> model. Under the hood it uses `ntm send --pane=W.1` (W.1 addressing verified; pane-base-index=1) or native type flags where they exist — one code path preferred for predictability. Generate `ntm-send-<short>` convenience aliases per agent FROM the table so names stay mechanically consistent. Keep ntm-cc/ntm-cod/ntm-gmi as thin aliases for muscle memory once adopt makes them work.

ACCEPTANCE: every launchable agent is messageable by one consistent name; B-team agents included; `ntm-to qwen ...` works; no duplicate names in any help/completion output (764.3.4 completions consume the same table — related).

title: Turn the static overview window into live mission control (ntm activity --watch or dashboard)
description:
PROBLEM: window 1 renders a banner once, then idles at a shell prompt forever — dead space that also hides `ntm activity --watch` (the genuinely useful view) behind a command nobody remembers.

DESIGN: after banner display (or instead of it, post-migration), auto-run a live view in window 1: `ntm activity <session> --watch`, or `ntm dashboard <session>`, or a tmux split with banner on top + activity below. Must degrade gracefully if the session has no typed agents yet (activity watch on an untyped session today shows little — verify what it renders pre/post migration).

CONSIDERATIONS: window 1 is also where _ntm_attach focuses; a live view there is the first thing seen on attach — that is the point. Keep a way to get a plain shell (e.g. the view runs in the pane but Ctrl-C drops to shell; document in banner footer).

ACCEPTANCE: attaching to a fresh team session lands on a self-updating agent-activity view; Ctrl-C yields a working shell in the right directory.

title: Replace fixed sleeps (sleep 1 / sleep 0.5 x3) with pane-readiness polling
description:
PROBLEM: launch path burns ~2.5s in fixed sleeps (.zshrc:153 sleep 0.5 per spawn x3; :234/:274 sleep 1) AND is still racy — send-keys into a not-yet-initialized interactive zsh loses keystrokes on a loaded box (symptom: a pane sitting at a bare prompt with no agent, needing manual intervention).

DESIGN: poll `tmux display-message -p -t <target> "#{pane_in_mode}/#{pane_current_command}"` or send a no-op marker and wait for the shell prompt to be ready (simplest robust trick: send-keys the source command repeatedly until `tmux capture-pane` shows the setup message, with a timeout + loud failure). NOTE: this task is ONLY relevant if the keystone decides to KEEP hand-rolled spawning; native ntm spawn has its own stagger/readiness logic. If migration lands, close this as obsolete with a comment.

ACCEPTANCE: cold `ntm-team` launch on an idle box is measurably faster AND 20 consecutive launches on a loaded box (stress -c) produce zero panes stuck at a bare prompt.

title: Guard against same-basename session collisions (two projects, one session name)
description:
PROBLEM: _ntm_target derives session name from sanitized directory BASENAME only (.zshrc:52-55). Two same-basename projects collide; launching in the second silently attaches to the FIRST project's session (.zshrc:219-223, 304-308).

DESIGN (unchanged core): record NTM_PROJECT_DIR at creation (tmux set-environment -t <s>); on has-session fast path compare vs $PWD; mismatch -> loud warn + offer attach-anyway / create deterministic suffixed session (api-<shorthash>) / abort. Same-dir re-run stays zero-friction.

PLAN-SPACE NOTE (2026-07-27): if 764.2.1 migrates launchers to native spawn, `ntm spawn --safety` ("Fail if session already exists", confirmed in --help) gives the collision DETECTION for free — the suffix/choice logic still lives in our launcher. So implement detection via --safety post-migration, via has-session probe until then.

ACCEPTANCE: two same-basename dirs produce two distinguishable sessions or an explicit choice; same-dir re-run still just attaches; existing ubuntu/roblox sessions unaffected.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Concrete walkthrough (do this once to feel the pain): mkdir -p /tmp/a/proj /tmp/b/proj; cd /tmp/a/proj && ntm-claude (session "proj" created, Claude launched on project A). cd /tmp/b/proj && ntm-claude -> "Session proj already exists. Attaching..." -> you are now typing project-B prompts into a Claude whose cwd is project A. No warning, and the project path shown in the banner is the ONLY clue. The set-environment probe in the description (NTM_PROJECT_DIR recorded at creation) makes the fix a 5-line comparison on the has-session fast path. Keep re-runs from the SAME directory zero-friction — that is the hot path and must stay one command.

title: Banner robustness: truncate long session/path values, cap width to terminal
description:
PROBLEM: _ntm_show_banner pads with %-50s (.zshrc:180-181) but never TRUNCATES — a session name or project path longer than 50 chars shoves the right border off-column and the box falls apart (printf pads, it does not clip). Deep paths like /home/ubuntu/Developer/some/long/project easily exceed 50. Width W=62 is also fixed, overflowing narrow terminals/split panes.

DESIGN: pre-truncate values in zsh with ellipsis ("${(r:47:)var%…}"-style or ${var:0:47}…), and derive W from `tput cols` clamped to a sane band (e.g. 50..76) with the banner centered or left-aligned consistently. Keep the box-drawing characters (═ ║ ╔) — they render fine — just make arithmetic hold for all rows (header/rule/data rows must ALL use the same computed inner width; the current mix of W-12/W-37 constants is why columns misalign when W changes).

ACCEPTANCE: banner renders a perfect rectangle with a 90-char path, a 3-char session name, and in an 80-col and a 45-col pane.
close_reason: Superseded by 764.2.10 (Banner v2). Plan-space revision: six beads were editing the same ~40-line _ntm_show_banner across three phases; consolidated into one coherent rewrite. Width/truncation scope moved there verbatim.

title: Read the tmux prefix hint live instead of hardcoding Ctrl+B
description:
PROBLEM: banner footer hardcodes "Navigate: Ctrl+B, then window number" (.zshrc:193). Verified correct TODAY (prefix is C-b), but ~/.tmux.conf is user-editable; the moment someone remaps the prefix, the onboarding hint in every session lies.

FIX: resolve at banner time: `tmux show-option -gqv prefix` (returns e.g. "C-b") and pretty-print (C-b -> Ctrl+B). One line. Also mention the F6 palette binding (ntm bind sets it; config palette_key = "F6") since it is the highest-value undiscovered feature — read it from `ntm config` if cheap, else keep static.

ACCEPTANCE: with prefix temporarily set to C-a in a scratch server, the banner says Ctrl+A.
close_reason: Superseded by 764.2.10 (Banner v2). Live prefix-hint scope moved there verbatim (one-line fix, but same function — consolidating to avoid edit churn).

title: Anchor nuke-session pkill to the abacusai binary and add a confirm
description:
PROBLEM (.zshrc:470-474): `pkill -u "$USER" -f "abacusai"` matches the substring ANYWHERE in any cmdline — an editor with /home/ubuntu/abacusai-notes/ open, a grep for abacusai, the agent_mail_send curl if the URL contained it — all die. The comment says "kills EVERY abacusai agent you own" but the pattern is broader than the documentation, and there is no confirmation for a command that also kills the tmux server (every session, every pane, unsaved state).

FIX: anchor to the executable: `pkill -u "$USER" -x abacusai` if the process name is exactly abacusai (verify with `pgrep -ax node | grep abacusai` — NOTE: panes run under `node` per tmux pane_current_command, so -x abacusai may match nothing; may need `-f "node.*abacusai"` tightened to the actual argv[0]/script path — inspect real cmdlines first: `pgrep -af abacusai`). Add a list-and-confirm: show what will die (count of agents + tmux sessions), require y. Keep --yes flag for scripts.

ACCEPTANCE: `pgrep -af abacusai` before/after shows ONLY intended processes died; running nuke-session with a decoy process named similarly leaves the decoy alive; non-interactive `nuke-session --yes` still works.

title: P2: Premium polish (pane titles, accent colors, startup speed, completions)
description:
Phase epic. "Stripe-level" feel: the workflow should look labeled, intentional and fast.

WHY LAST: polish applied before the P1 spawn-migration decision risks polishing deleted code. Each child declares its dependency on P1 explicitly.

BAR: every visual element must be data-driven (from the unified team table, not hardcoded), must survive narrow terminals, and must not add measurable startup latency to panes (every agent pane is an interactive zsh that sources .zshrc, so shell-startup cost multiplies by pane count).

title: Per-pane display titles (Persona · Model) — mostly delivered by adopt; this adds the rich names
description:
RESCOPE (2026-07-27): two probe findings shrink this task. (1) ~/.tmux.conf pane-border-format ALREADY renders #{pane_title} with a colored active-pane marker — zero tmux.conf change needed. (2) `ntm adopt` (wired into launchers by 764.1.10) AUTO-SETS pane titles to {session}__{type}_{n} — so basic labeled borders arrive FREE at P0.

WHAT REMAINS HERE: upgrade titles from machine names (ubuntu__cc_1) to human display names ("BlueCastle · Claude Sonnet 4.6", overview pane -> "Overview · mission control"). Persona/display names come from the unified team table — hence dep on 764.2.2 (replaces the old keystone dep: titles now survive BOTH keystone outcomes because adopt sets baseline titles either way). Set via `tmux select-pane -t <session>:W.1 -T "<title>"` after adopt; verify adopt does not later overwrite custom titles (if it does, order: adopt first, then re-title).

ACCEPTANCE: every pane in a fresh team session shows "Persona · Model" in its top border; overview labeled; survives window renames; no empty borders.
close_reason: DONE (user-direct request): premium pane headings live. (1) _NTM_PANE_META seed table in .zshrc (model-id -> display|accent|type, Catppuccin Mocha accents: claude=peach #fab387, codex=green #a6e3a1, gemini=blue #89b4fa, zai=yellow, qwen=teal, grok=mauve) — this is the proto-table 764.2.2 will generalize; zero call-site duplication. (2) _ntm_spawn_agent records @agent_persona/@agent_model pane vars; _ntm_beautify_panes (called after ntm adopt in all 3 launchers) sets per-pane pane-border-format with active-diamond indicator + 'Persona · Display Model' bold title, dim pane-border-style, accent pane-active-border-style. Overview windows get 'Mission Control · session' in lavender ◈. (3) tmux.conf: pane-border-lines heavy (rounded unsupported in this build), vaporware comment replaced with pointer. VERIFIED on throwaway session (titles, 4 distinct per-pane formats + active border styles all correct) AND applied to live ubuntu+roblox sessions in place — all 8 panes re-titled. zsh -n passes.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DEPENDENCY OVERRIDE (2026-07-28): removing the blocker on 764.2.2 (team table) because the user directly requested pane-title beautification now. Drift risk is neutralized by design: implementing a seed mapping _NTM_PANE_META (model-id -> display|accent|type) in .zshrc which BECOMES the proto-table that 764.2.2 will later generalize — display names are NOT copied to call sites. Verified on tmux 3.5a: per-pane pane-border-format AND pane-border-style are settable (premium per-agent accent headings are possible); pane-border-lines rounded unsupported in this build (heavy works). — CalmRobin

title: Per-agent accent colors: banner rows + per-session status-style, driven by the team table
description:
VISION: today the whole banner is one flat cyan (A-team) / magenta (B-team). Premium feel = each agent row tinted a distinct accent (e.g. Claude warm orange, GPT green, Gemini blue — echoing brand associations), with the SAME accent reused as that pane's border color (tmux select-pane -P / pane-active-border-style per window where supported) so color = identity everywhere. Session-level status-style tint distinguishes A-team vs B-team when switching clients.

DESIGN: colors MUST come from the unified team table (764.2.2) as a per-agent field — no third copy of agent metadata. Use 256-color or truecolor guarded by `tput colors` fallback so it degrades cleanly over SSH/tmux-256color.

CONSIDERATIONS: keep contrast WCAG-ish readable on dark terminals; test against the Catppuccin mocha palette already used by status-style in tmux.conf so accents harmonize rather than clash.

ACCEPTANCE: banner rows, pane borders, and pane titles share one per-agent accent; readable in 256-color and 16-color fallback.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: PARTIAL DELIVERY (2026-07-28, via 764.3.1): the pane-side half of this bead is DONE — per-agent accent colors now live in pane headings (border-format text + pane-active-border-style per pane, Catppuccin Mocha, driven by _NTM_PANE_META). REMAINING for this bead: (a) per-agent accent ROWS in the banner (gated on 764.2.10 Banner v2 — apply colors there, do NOT touch current banner), (b) per-session status-style tint to distinguish A-team vs B-team when switching clients. Leaving open. — CalmRobin

title: Cut shell startup cost: cache 'ntm shell zsh' output, skip redundant 'ntm bind'
description:
PROBLEM: every agent pane is an interactive zsh sourcing .zshrc, so startup cost MULTIPLIES by pane count. Each shell runs `eval "$(ntm shell zsh)"` (forks ntm, ~tens of ms) and `ntm bind` (idempotent tmux keybinding write — pointless in every pane and after the first shell).

DESIGN: cache the `ntm shell zsh` output to ~/.cache/ntm/shell-init.zsh, regenerated only when the ntm binary mtime/sha changes or the cache is older than N days; source the cache. Run `ntm bind` only when NOT in tmux pane context and once per boot/tmux-server (guard via a sentinel in tmux server env or a stamp file). Measure before/after with `time zsh -i -c exit` (hyperfine if available).

Core loop: `cass search "<query>" --robot --limit 5 --fields minimal` -> `cass view <source_path> -n <line> --json` -> `cass expand <source_path> -n <line> -C 3 --json`.

title: TABC MVP v1: automated weekly license-application lead delivery
description: Build a lean B2B data-product MVP that automatically queries TABC public license/application data, extracts new filings from the last seven days, cleans and prioritizes the records, writes them to Google Sheets, and emails subscribers every Monday morning. The strategic intent is to validate whether recent TABC activity is a monetizable buying signal before investing in a full SaaS application. This root bead owns the complete founder roadmap, technical delivery path, validation path, and operational guardrails.
design: Keep v1 intentionally simple: scheduled Python pipeline, raw-data retention, cleaned lead output, Google Sheets as the delivery surface, and email as the notification layer. Optimize for the buyer job-to-be-done: help vendors and service providers discover newly licensed or soon-to-open alcohol-related businesses early enough to take timely sales action. Avoid web app, login, billing portal, dashboards, complex CRM integrations, or AI scoring until paid pilots confirm demand.
acceptance_criteria: MVP is considered complete when: (1) the pipeline can run on schedule without manual raw-data handling, (2) at least one target county produces records or explicitly reports no new records with an alert, (3) Current Week and Archive sheet tabs are updated correctly, (4) a Monday email with top hot leads is delivered, (5) pilot prospects can review real data, (6) the lead list is understandable without founder explanation, and (7) pilot success thresholds are defined before launch.
notes: Overarching success metric: prove customers will pay for a reliable weekly lead list. Technical sophistication is secondary to repeatable delivery, buyer actionability, and customer learning.

title: Map TABC search flow, data endpoints, and constraints
description: Investigate how tabc.texas.gov exposes license/application search results. Determine whether records are available through static HTML, JSON/network calls, downloadable files, or JavaScript-rendered pages requiring browser automation. Capture pagination behavior, search parameters, session requirements, rate limits, CAPTCHA or bot controls, and source URLs for traceability.
design: Use browser devtools and small manual probes. Prefer non-browser HTTP requests if the site exposes stable HTML or JSON; use Playwright only if necessary. Record observations in the bead so future maintainers understand why the chosen approach was selected.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: identified access method; known required inputs; known result fields; pagination behavior understood; constraints and risks recorded; at least one reproducible manual query path exists.
notes: Important consideration: avoid aggressive scraping. The MVP needs a weekly low-volume run, not high-throughput crawling.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if TABC changes its site, this bead should contain the original assumptions to compare against the new behavior.

comments.author: PearlMountain
comments.text:
Completed source mapping findings:

Access method:
- Official entry point is https://apps.tabc.texas.gov/publicinquiry/.
- First request redirects/serves TABCRegulatoryAgreement.aspx. User must acknowledge the regulatory agreement before using the system.
- The app is ASP.NET WebForms. Navigation and form submission use cookies plus __VIEWSTATE, __EVENTVALIDATION, __EVENTTARGET, and related hidden fields. This is not a static HTML or simple JSON API surface.
- Low-volume HTTP form posts can reproduce the flow if the session cookie and hidden fields are preserved, but implementation should treat Playwright as likely safer unless Requests/BeautifulSoup proves stable during implementation.

Primary MVP query path:
1. Open Public Inquiry System.
2. Acknowledge regulatory agreement.
3. From Default.aspx choose Application(s) Status Related Inquiries -> Create a list of Application(s).
4. On ApplicationRoster.aspx enter required criteria:
   - Step 1 Location: county/city/ZIP, e.g. HARRIS, All Cities, All Zip Codes.
   - Step 2 License Type: add at least one license type, e.g. AIMS Tier Retail -> MB-R Mixed Beverage Permit.
   - Step 3 Status: Pending - In Review and/or Received.
   - Step 4 Application Submission Date: optional start/end dates.
5. Go to ApplicationRosterSummary.aspx.
6. Choose output type: Report Document (PDF), Excel File, or Comma-Delimited File.
7. Complete CAPTCHA and submit query.

Required inputs and constraints:
- Steps 1-3 are required.
- Step 1 or Step 2 must contain an entry that does not call all records.
- Location supports county, city, ZIP; county list includes all Texas counties. Harris/Dallas/Travis can be selected directly.
- License type selection is dynamic. AIMS Tier Retail exposes BE-R, BF-R, BG-R, BP-S, BQ-R, E-S, FB-S, LH-S, LP-S, MB-R, N-R, NB-R, NE-R, NT-R, P-R, Q-R, TR-R, WP-S.
- Status values observed: Pending - In Review (value 3) and Received (value 2).
- Date fields are application submission start/end dates, optional, likely used to narrow to last 7 days.
- Summary/export step has CAPTCHA explicitly labeled Security Measures (This helps to prevent automated searches.).

Result/export behavior:
- Application roster does not expose result rows directly before CAPTCHA.
- Summary page offers PDF, Excel, and CSV outputs after CAPTCHA.
- The page links official record layout at https://www.tabc.texas.gov/static/sites/default/files/2022-10/public-roster-original-application-layout.pdf.
- Web fetch could not extract the PDF fields because the PDF appears image/binary-heavy; field inventory should be finalized by direct PDF review/OCR or by a manual CSV/Excel sample.

Known fields from UI/search context:
- Location: county, city, ZIP.
- License type/tier/class.
- Status.
- Application submission date.
- Output likely includes application/license identifiers, applicant/owner/trade name, location/address/county, license type, status, and application dates, but exact column names must come from record layout or sample export.

Pagination/download:
- No ordinary HTML pagination was reached for application results. Export output is selected before final CAPTCHA-protected submit.
- For MVP, prefer CSV/Excel output parsing if a compliant/manual CAPTCHA handling path is acceptable; otherwise use open-records/manual export or a human-in-the-loop source capture until an acceptable automated path is confirmed.

Risks and constraints:
- CAPTCHA is a material anti-automation control. Do not bypass it.
- Use is monitored/recorded/audited; unauthorized use is prohibited.
- Site may be unavailable Tuesdays 6pm-11pm CST.
- Data is updated daily and should be timely within 24 hours.
- Public Inquiry says pending original application data only; pending renewal applications are under license status secondary status.
- Open Data Portal has TABC License Information for issued/approved licenses, but public search results found it describes approved licenses, not pending original applications, so it is not a complete substitute for this MVP lead source.

Recommendation for dependent bead 2.1:
- First implementation choice should not assume a stable unauthenticated API.
- Build a source adapter abstraction.
- Treat direct HTTP WebForms replay as possible but brittle.
- Prefer a compliance-friendly acquisition strategy: manual weekly export upload or approved access path for v1 if CAPTCHA blocks automation; only use Playwright for normal navigation, not CAPTCHA bypass.

title: Define minimum viable TABC lead field inventory
description: Create the canonical v1 field list for raw and cleaned records. Minimum useful fields: business_name, license_type, status, application_date, address, city, state, zip, county, applicant_name, source_url, scraped_at, week_of, plus cleaned/enriched fields such as clean_business_name, formatted_address, days_since_filing, concept_category, lead_score, and is_hot_lead.
design: Separate raw fields from cleaned fields. Raw fields preserve source truth for debugging; cleaned fields support customer usability. Do not add fields unless they are visible in the source, trivially derived, or directly tied to the target buyer workflow. Include record identity and confidence/missingness considerations so downstream publishing can avoid duplicate or misleading rows.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: v1 field contract is explicit; required vs optional fields are marked; types/date formats are defined; missing-data behavior is described; source_url or equivalent traceability is included; record identity inputs are identified; customer-facing columns map to user decisions.
notes: This becomes the contract shared by scraper, cleaner, sheet writer, tests, pilot feedback, and data-quality validation.
close_reason: Completed: defined source-confirmed raw fields, cleaned/customer fields, metadata, types, missing-data behavior, identity/dedupe inputs, and customer decision mapping.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: a clear data contract prevents downstream scripts from each inventing their own shape and makes site-change debugging much faster.

comments.author: PearlMountain
comments.text:
Completed v1 field inventory / data contract:

Source-confirmed raw fields from TABC Public Roster Record Layout for Pending Original New Application(s):
1. master_file_id: string/integer-like, optional but preferred; reference number associated with all licenses held by one legal owner entity.
2. application_id: string/integer-like, required when present in export; unique numerical reference to an AIMS application. Primary record identity input.
3. license_type: string, required; current TABC primary/subordinate license type, max two characters in the official layout, e.g. MB, BG, BQ.
4. application_status: enum string, required; Public Inquiry includes Received and In Review.
5. primary_license_id: string/integer-like, optional; may be blank until application approval unless existing primary license is associated with a new subordinate application.
6. subordinate_license_id: string/integer-like, optional; may be blank until approval.
7. submission_date: date, required for MVP filtering when available; date AIMS application was submitted to TABC.
8. trade_name: string, optional but customer-important; establishment/DBA.
9. owner_name: string, optional but customer-important; owner submitting the application.
10. wine_percent: string/integer enum 14/17, optional; applicable only to certain license classes.
11. gun_sign: enum Blue/Red, optional; Red indicates required red handgun warning sign.
12. address: string, optional but customer-important; physical location street number/name.
13. address_2: string, optional; suite or additional physical-location details.
14. city: string, optional but customer-important.
15. state: string, optional; expected TX for Texas locations.
16. zip: string, optional; no hyphen per layout.
17. phone: string, optional; business phone number.
18. county: string, required for scoped MVP runs; Texas county associated with physical licensed location.
19. country: string, optional; country associated with physical licensed location.

Operational/source metadata fields to add at ingestion:
- source_system: constant string, e.g. tabc_public_inquiry_application_roster.
- source_url: string, required; use https://apps.tabc.texas.gov/publicinquiry/ApplicationRosterSummary.aspx or the stable Public Inquiry URL plus search criteria when row-level URL is unavailable.
- source_record_layout_url: string, required constant: https://www.tabc.texas.gov/static/sites/default/files/2022-10/public-roster-original-application-layout.pdf.
- query_county: string, required; configured county used for the run.
- query_license_types: array/string, required; license type criteria used.
- query_statuses: array/string, required; Received and/or In Review.
- query_start_date/query_end_date: date, required for a scheduled run.
- scraped_at: datetime UTC ISO-8601, required.
- week_of: date ISO YYYY-MM-DD, required; Monday start date for weekly delivery.
- source_file_name/source_file_hash: string, required when ingesting a manual CSV/Excel export; supports traceability and dedupe.

Cleaned/customer-facing fields:
- business_name: string, required for display; prefer trade_name, fallback owner_name, fallback application_id label.
- clean_business_name: string, required; normalized business_name for dedupe/display.
- applicant_name: string, optional; map from owner_name for MVP terminology.
- formatted_address: string, optional; address + address_2 + city + state + zip.
- location_key: string, optional; normalized address/city/state/zip/county for dedupe.
- days_since_filing: integer, required; computed from submission_date to run date.
- filing_recency_bucket: enum 0-2/3-7/8+ days, optional but useful for ranking.
- concept_category: enum/string, optional; simple heuristic from trade_name/license_type, e.g. restaurant_bar, package_store, brewery, private_club, unknown.
- lead_score: integer 0-100, required for hot lead sorting; v1 heuristic based on recency, county, license type, and field completeness.
- is_hot_lead: boolean, required; true when lead_score exceeds configured threshold or rule set.
- missing_required_fields: array/string, required; records field-quality issues without silently dropping rows.
- data_quality_notes: string, optional; human-readable concerns.

Record identity and dedupe:
- Primary identity: application_id when present.
- Secondary identity: master_file_id + license_type + submission_date + normalized address/county when application_id is missing.
- Display duplicate guard: clean_business_name + location_key + license_type + submission_date.
- Do not merge separate application_id values even if owner/location match; multiple licenses for one business can be meaningful leads.

Missing-data behavior:
- Do not reject records solely for missing trade_name, owner_name, phone, address_2, wine_percent, gun_sign, primary_license_id, subordinate_license_id, or country.
- Records missing application_id must carry a generated provisional identity and a data_quality_notes warning.
- Records missing submission_date cannot be included in last-7-days delivery unless manually verified; mark as invalid_for_weekly_filter.
- Records outside configured counties should be excluded from customer delivery but may be archived for debugging only if intentionally collected.

Customer decision mapping:
- business_name/trade_name/owner_name: tells buyer who to research/contact.
- license_type/status/submission_date/days_since_filing: tells buyer why the lead is timely and relevant.
- address/city/county/zip/formatted_address: tells buyer territory and visit/contact routing.
- phone: direct outreach if present.
- concept_category/lead_score/is_hot_lead: prioritizes Monday email and sheet sorting.
- source metadata: lets founder/debugger trace any row back to TABC export and query assumptions.

title: Choose initial county and subscriber scope
description: Select the first geography for MVP delivery. Recommended scope is one to three high-value counties rather than statewide. Candidate counties include Harris, Dallas, and Travis, but final choice should reflect buyer concentration, density of alcohol license activity, and founder access to prospects.
design: Initial geography: start with Harris, Dallas, and Travis as the default three-county pilot bundle, with permission to substitute a prospect-requested county if a serious buyer needs it for evaluation. Rationale: these counties represent the Houston, Dallas, and Austin markets, are likely to have dense restaurant/bar activity, and align with sales territories that alcohol distributors, brand reps, POS/payment vendors, and insurance/compliance sellers can understand quickly. Avoid statewide coverage for v1 because it increases scraping, QA, dedupe, sheet size, and support burden before demand is proven. Customer scope: 1-3 pilot customers, each receiving either one county or the same three-county bundle, configured manually.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance met: initial county list is Harris, Dallas, and Travis; rationale is recorded; statewide and long-tail counties are intentionally deferred; pilot customer assumptions are tied to beachhead alcohol-distributor/brand-rep and adjacent vendor workflows; substitution rule is defined for serious prospects.
notes: Decision rule: if a likely paid pilot asks for a specific Texas county, choose that county over abstract market-size logic. Otherwise use Harris/Dallas/Travis as the first sample because recognizable metro coverage makes buyer interviews easier. Keep county count small until source reliability, sheet usability, and customer actionability are proven. Deferred scope: statewide, all counties, historical backfills beyond sample needs, and custom territory management.
close_reason: Completed: selected Harris/Dallas/Travis default scope, defined prospect-driven substitution rule, deferred statewide coverage, and tied scope to ICP workflow.

title: Interview 5 target buyers with sample sheet
description: Show the sample TABC lead list to five likely customers such as vendors serving bars/restaurants, real estate brokers, alcohol distributors, compliance consultants, POS providers, payroll providers, insurance brokers, or local marketing agencies. Ask what they would do with the list, which fields are missing, what counties matter, and whether they would pay for weekly delivery.

title: Cross-cutting guardrails: compliance, ethics, privacy, and scope control
description: Maintain safe, legal, and focused operation of the MVP. Respect public-data terms, avoid excessive scraping, protect credentials, prevent accidental public data exposure, and resist premature expansion into a full SaaS platform.
design: Guardrails should be lightweight but explicit. They protect the company from operational, legal, and reputational problems while keeping the team focused on validation.
acceptance_criteria: Done when scraping etiquette, secret handling, sheet-sharing/privacy, and v1 scope boundaries are recorded and checked before pilot launch.

title: Review TABC terms, robots, and acceptable-use constraints
