title: Define ICP, buyer job-to-be-done, and weekly use case
description: Define the initial ideal customer profile and the concrete job the weekly TABC list helps them perform. Candidate users include alcohol distributors, POS vendors, payroll/HR vendors, insurance brokers, restaurant equipment suppliers, marketing agencies, commercial real estate brokers, compliance consultants, and lenders serving bars/restaurants. Clarify who buys, who opens the sheet, what action they take after seeing a lead, and what makes a lead worth paying for.
design: Beachhead ICP: sales teams that sell directly to newly opening or changing Texas bars/restaurants and can act quickly from a weekly lead list. Rank initial segments: (1) alcohol distributors and brand reps, because TABC activity maps directly to their selling motion and they already think in licenses, counties, and accounts; (2) POS/payment/payroll vendors serving restaurants/bars, because new openings have clear setup needs; (3) insurance brokers and compliance consultants, because license/application events imply operational needs. Defer real estate brokers, lenders, marketing agencies, equipment suppliers, and broad statewide data buyers until pilot evidence shows demand. Primary buyer/user workflow: Monday email arrives, user reviews the top hot leads, opens the Google Sheet, filters by county/license/status/concept, identifies likely new opening or ownership-change opportunities, checks source link/raw fields if needed, assigns or contacts the account, and marks whether the lead was useful. Product decisions should optimize for fast qualification and outreach, not exhaustive research.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance met: initial ICP is ranked with alcohol distributors/brand reps as beachhead; primary weekly workflow is described from Monday email to outreach action; must-have columns are tied to user actions; non-target users are explicitly deferred; success criteria emphasize customer actionability and sales behavior, not only technical delivery.
notes: Must-have sheet/email fields for the beachhead: business/legal name, trade name if available, address/city/county/zip, application date, days since filing, status, license/application type, applicant/entity/owner if available, source URL, concept category, lead score/hot-lead rank, record ID/dedupe key, run date/date window, notes/useful? feedback column. Hot-lead logic should initially privilege recency and actionable stage; do not assume Approved is always best until buyer interviews confirm timing. User-action success signals: customer opens sheet, filters or replies with useful rows, contacts at least one lead, asks for more counties/categories, or agrees to pay/continue. Non-goals for v1: generic statewide database, polished CRM, enrichment-heavy prospect profiles, and supporting every possible buyer segment at once.
close_reason: Completed: ranked beachhead ICP, weekly user workflow, action-oriented field needs, deferred segments, and customer actionability success signals.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if the buyer is a distributor, they may care about license type and approval timing. If the buyer is a broker, they may care more about address, operator, and stage. Pick a beachhead before optimizing every use case.

comments.author: SilverRiver
comments.text: Completed ICP/JTBD decision in plan space. Chose alcohol distributors/brand reps as the initial beachhead because TABC application/license events are closest to their sales trigger, while POS/payroll/payment vendors and insurance/compliance providers remain strong secondary pilots. Future implementation should optimize the sheet and email for qualification-to-outreach speed: what changed, where, how fresh, what license/status, who might be contacted, and why this row is worth action.

title: Define pilot success metrics and kill criteria before launch
description: Define measurable criteria for whether the MVP is working commercially and operationally before launching pilots. Include activation, engagement, payment, retention, data reliability, and qualitative actionability thresholds. Also define kill/pivot criteria so the team does not rationalize weak demand after implementation.
design: Pilot success framework: evaluate both commercial pull and operational reliability before v2 investment. Success means the beachhead buyer can repeatedly turn the Monday sheet into sales action with minimal founder explanation. Primary pilot target: alcohol distributors/brand reps in 1-3 Texas counties, with secondary learning from POS/payment/payroll or insurance/compliance buyers only if they are easy to access. Measure five dimensions: activation, actionability, willingness to pay, retention/engagement, and data operations quality. Decisions should be made after a defined pilot window, not after isolated anecdotes.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance met: explicit success metrics are defined; explicit kill/pivot criteria are defined; metrics must be agreed before pilot delivery; v2 decision references these thresholds; thresholds include user behavior and commercial signals, not only build completion.
notes: Go criteria for continuing after pilot: at least 3 of 5 target prospects say a sample/current sheet contains actionable leads; at least 1 paid pilot or clear written willingness to pay at the proposed price; at least 1 pilot reports contacting or assigning a lead from the sheet; two consecutive weekly runs complete without manual raw-data handling or critical data-quality incidents; weekly sheet/email can be understood without founder walkthrough; customer asks are incremental improvements rather than fundamental confusion about value. Kill or major pivot criteria: fewer than 2 of 5 target prospects find sample rows actionable; no prospect is willing to pay or commit after seeing real data; customers say data arrives too late for their workflow and no earlier source/status is available; source data cannot be accessed reliably or legally at low volume; weekly operation requires recurring manual raw-data cleanup; repeated data-quality issues damage trust. Pivot options: change buyer segment, change county/source scope, prioritize earlier application statuses over Approved, sell concierge research instead of automated list, or stop if TABC signal is weak.
close_reason: Completed: defined activation, actionability, payment, retention, reliability, go/pivot/kill thresholds, and v2 decision discipline.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: plan space is where we decide what evidence matters. Once the pipeline exists, it is tempting to keep adding features even if buyers are not engaging.

comments.author: SilverRiver
comments.text: Completed pilot success/kill framework. The most important founder discipline is separating technical completion from market validation: a working scraper is not success unless customers take action, pay, and trust the weekly delivery. Use these thresholds before approving v2 scope.

title: Phase 2: design lean MVP architecture and repository foundation
description: Establish the smallest reliable technical foundation for the pipeline: Python scripts, configuration, data contracts, secret handling, run modes, logging conventions, and project structure. The purpose is to make later build tasks straightforward without introducing SaaS-level complexity.
design: Architecture should remain a linear batch pipeline: scrape raw data, persist raw data, clean records, write sheets, send email, and emit logs/alerts. Each step should be runnable independently for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Done when repo structure, runtime/dependency choices, configuration strategy, and local run contract are defined well enough for implementation tasks to proceed.
notes: Prefer explicit scripts over frameworks. Future maintainers should be able to run one command and inspect intermediate files.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the MVP operational risk is silent weekly failure. A simple pipeline with observable intermediate artifacts is easier to trust than an over-abstracted system.

title: Choose Requests/BeautifulSoup versus Playwright implementation path
description: Decide whether the scraper should use direct HTTP parsing with requests and BeautifulSoup or browser automation with Playwright. The decision must be based on the source-data mapping rather than preference. Direct HTTP is preferred for simplicity and deployability; Playwright is acceptable if the site requires JavaScript-rendered interactions.
design: Use a Python source-adapter architecture for v1: core ingestion reads approved/manual-assisted CSV or Excel exports and normalizes them into the MVP pipeline. Keep requests + BeautifulSoup for parsing static/approved documents only. Keep Playwright optional and manual-assisted for normal browser navigation/export workflows only; do not use it to bypass CAPTCHA or automate prohibited access.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: selected stack is recorded; trade-offs are documented; deployment implications are noted; fallback path is identified if the first stack becomes brittle.
notes: Decision is based on completed source mapping: TABC Public Inquiry is stateful ASP.NET WebForms with acknowledgement gate, hidden state fields, and CAPTCHA constraints around export/search-summary behavior. This makes unattended direct WebForms replay brittle and compliance-sensitive. Core v1 deployment should not require browsers; fallback is approved access/manual upload until a stable official endpoint exists.
close_reason: Completed: selected compliance-friendly Python source-adapter/manual-or-approved-export path; documented Requests/BeautifulSoup vs Playwright trade-offs, deployment implications, and fallback.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if Playwright is chosen, account for heavier CI/VPS setup, browser dependencies, and slower runs.

comments.author: PearlMountain
comments.text:
Decision recorded for v1 implementation path:

Selected path: compliance-friendly source adapter around approved exports/manual-assisted CSV or Excel input, implemented in Python with tabular parsing and normalization as the core pipeline. Do not build an unattended CAPTCHA-bypassing scraper for v1.

Rationale from source mapping: TABC Public Inquiry behaves like ASP.NET WebForms, with acknowledgement-gate state, __VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION, event targets, and CAPTCHA around export/search-summary behavior. Direct requests + BeautifulSoup form replay would be brittle and operationally risky because it depends on opaque stateful postbacks and may run into the CAPTCHA boundary. Playwright can model browser navigation, but using it for unattended collection would not remove the compliance constraint and would increase deployment complexity.

Trade-offs: Python requests/BeautifulSoup remains useful for static pages, metadata inspection, and parsing any approved/downloaded HTML. The main production path should be a source adapter that ingests operator-provided or officially approved exports, then transforms rows into the MVP schema. Playwright is allowed only as an optional manual-assisted navigation/export helper for normal browser workflows where a human handles acknowledgements and CAPTCHA; it must not solve, outsource, or evade CAPTCHA.

Deployment implications: v1 can run as a lightweight scheduled Python job without browser dependencies for the core pipeline. Avoiding mandatory Playwright keeps GitHub Actions/VPS deployment simpler, cheaper, and easier to debug. If a manual-assisted helper is later required, isolate it as a non-scheduled utility with explicit human-in-the-loop operation and separate browser dependency setup.

Fallback path: if official/approved export access is unavailable or manual export cadence is too burdensome, pause full automation and pursue a TABC-approved data access route, public records/export arrangement, or founder-defined manual upload process. If TABC later provides a stable API or non-CAPTCHA export endpoint, add a new source adapter behind the same ingestion interface.

title: Create minimal pipeline-oriented repository structure
description: Define or create the code organization for scripts and data artifacts. Suggested structure: src/scrape_tabc.py, src/clean_records.py, src/write_sheets.py, src/send_email.py, src/config.py, data/raw, data/cleaned, tests, requirements or pyproject, and a scheduled workflow file later.
design: Keep modules separable by pipeline stage. Avoid introducing a web framework or database unless later evidence demands it.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: repository has a clear place for each pipeline stage; raw and cleaned data paths are separated; secrets are excluded from source control; README-level knowledge is encoded in bead notes if no docs are desired.
notes: Do not create documentation files unless explicitly requested; beads can carry the planning context.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: separate stages allow a failed sheet write to be retried without re-scraping and allow raw data to be inspected independently.

title: Define configuration and secrets strategy
description: Specify how counties, date windows, spreadsheet IDs, Google credentials, email provider keys, sender/recipient lists, and runtime flags are configured. Use environment variables or a local ignored config file for secrets; use GitHub Actions secrets or VPS environment variables in production.
design: Separate safe static config from secrets. The code should fail early with clear messages when required configuration is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: required config variables are listed; local dev and scheduled-run setup are defined; no credentials are committed; config validation behavior is specified.
notes: This protects pilot delivery and reduces setup mistakes during handoff.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: spreadsheet IDs and county lists are product configuration, not code logic. Keep them changeable without editing scraper internals.

title: Define data contract tests and fixture strategy
description: Create the test strategy for verifying raw and cleaned record shape, date parsing, required columns, deduplication keys, status values, and Google Sheet column order. Use small real-like fixtures derived from the manual sample while avoiding sensitive credentials.
design: Tests should focus on business-critical transformations and schema stability rather than mocking every integration. Fixture data should represent realistic TABC records and edge cases such as missing address parts or non-Approved statuses.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: required tests are enumerated; fixture approach is defined; schema validation covers raw and cleaned outputs; sheet column order has a test or explicit assertion.
notes: These tests are especially important because customer trust depends on consistent weekly columns.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: even a lightweight MVP needs guardrails around data shape because sheets are the customer-facing product surface.

title: Define stable record identity and deduplication strategy
description: Define how the system identifies the same TABC filing across runs, archive appends, retries, and possible source changes. Prefer a source-provided application/license identifier if available. If not available, use a documented composite key such as business name, address, application date, license type, county, and applicant/entity name.
design: Use a single canonical record_id everywhere. Prefer source_system + raw source application/license/record ID. If absent, generate a deterministic hash from preserved raw values plus normalized components for name, DBA, address, city, county, filing/application date, license type, status, and applicant/entity where available. Store raw fields, normalized key components, and record_id for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: primary record key is defined; fallback composite key is defined; duplicate handling behavior is documented; archive append and hot lead selection use the same identity; tests or fixtures cover rerun dedupe.
notes: Duplicate handling: collapse duplicates within a run, skip existing record_id values on Archive append, regenerate Current Week from the latest cleaned run, and use the same record_id for hot lead selection/email/backfill. Tests must cover source-ID reruns, fallback formatting differences, changed non-key fields, exact duplicates, and near-collisions. Future source-ID migration must avoid duplicating historical archive rows.
close_reason: Completed: defined primary source-ID key, fallback composite hash, duplicate behavior, archive/hot-lead consistency, collision handling, and fixture coverage.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if the source later exposes a better identifier, migrate keys carefully and do not silently duplicate historical archive rows.

comments.author: PearlMountain
comments.text:
Deduplication strategy for v1:

Primary identity: use a stable source-provided TABC application/license/record identifier when the export or approved source includes one. Store it exactly as raw_source_id and use record_id = source_system + ':' + raw_source_id after trimming surrounding whitespace only. Never rewrite the raw identifier.

Fallback composite identity: when no stable source ID exists, compute a deterministic hash over normalized key components: business/legal name, DBA/name if present, street address, city, county, application or filing date, license/permit type, application status, and applicant/entity name when present. Normalize by lowercasing, trimming, collapsing whitespace, removing punctuation that does not change meaning, standardizing common address tokens only if the raw value is also preserved, and parsing dates to ISO format. Keep both raw fields and normalized key components for auditability.

Duplicate behavior: within one run, collapse rows with the same record_id and retain the most complete row while recording duplicate_count/source row references in raw/debug output. Across reruns, Archive append must skip rows whose record_id already exists. Current Week should be regenerated from the latest cleaned run, not appended blindly. If the same record_id reappears with changed non-key fields, keep the archive row stable for first-seen history and optionally update Current Week with latest values.

Archive and hot-lead consistency: Archive append, Current Week replacement, hot lead selection, email excerpts, and backfill/rerun logic must all use the same record_id. Hot lead ranking must not create a separate identity concept.

Collision and migration handling: if fallback composite collisions are discovered, emit a loud validation error and include the conflicting raw rows for review rather than silently merging different businesses. If a better TABC identifier appears later, add a key migration step that maps old fallback IDs to new source IDs and prevents historical duplicate archive rows.

Test/fixture requirement: fixtures should include an exact duplicate row, a rerun with the same source ID, a fallback composite duplicate with formatting differences, a changed non-key field, and a near-collision where two distinct records share most fields but differ by date/license/address/applicant.

title: Design simple customer/county delivery configuration
description: Define the minimal configuration model for pilots: customer name, recipient emails, counties, spreadsheet ID or sheet URL, delivery mode, active/inactive status, and optional notes. Keep it file/env driven for v1 rather than building accounts or an admin UI.
design: Use file/env driven configuration for v1: a private runtime config contains a list of customer entries, while secrets stay in environment variables or excluded secret files. Each customer entry includes customer_id, name, active flag, counties, delivery mode, spreadsheet target, sheet tab names, recipients, timezone/schedule, hot-lead limit, and notes/tags. No database or admin UI for v1.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: config fields are defined; sensitive versus non-sensitive values are separated; inactive customers can be skipped; multiple customers/counties are representable; local test customer is supported.
notes: Sensitive values: service-account credentials, email API/OAuth credentials, sender secrets, and private sheet permissions must not be committed. Runtime should skip inactive customers, support multiple customers and multi-county scopes, include a local_test customer/dry-run mode, validate active configs before delivery, and carry customer_id through sheet/email steps to prevent cross-customer sends.
close_reason: Completed: defined v1 customer/county config fields, secret separation, inactive-skip behavior, multi-customer/multi-county support, local test customer, delivery modes, and validation rules.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the moment there is a second pilot customer, hard-coded sheet IDs and recipients become risky. Solve this in plan space with simple config, not a database.

comments.author: PearlMountain
comments.text:
Pilot configuration model for v1:

Use a simple checked-in example config plus an untracked local/production config file, not a database or admin UI. Recommended shape is a list of customers/accounts with explicit delivery targets and source scope.

Non-sensitive customer config fields: customer_id, customer_name, active, counties, delivery_mode, spreadsheet_id or spreadsheet_url, sheet_tabs/current_week/archive, recipient_emails, cc_emails, timezone, send_day, send_time_local, max_hot_leads, notes, and optional tags such as pilot/cohort. Counties should be a list so one customer can receive multiple counties and multiple customers can overlap counties.

Sensitive configuration/secrets: Google service account JSON or credential path, email provider API keys/OAuth tokens, sender account credentials, and any private spreadsheet permissions must come from environment variables or a secrets file excluded from source control. Customer recipient emails can live in the private runtime config for pilots; only sanitized examples should be committed.

Runtime behavior: inactive customers are skipped with an info log, not treated as errors. The pipeline should support one local test customer that writes to a test spreadsheet and can use a dry-run/no-email delivery mode. Each run should iterate active customers, collect/clean records for that customer county scope, write that customer's sheet, and send only to that customer's configured recipients.

Delivery modes: support at least dry_run, sheets_only, and sheets_and_email. This lets founder/operator validate data before enabling outbound email.

Validation rules: fail fast when an active customer lacks counties, sheet target, or required delivery credentials for its delivery_mode. Warn but continue when an inactive customer is incomplete. Validate recipient email format before sending. Prevent accidental cross-customer delivery by passing customer_id through sheet-writing and email-rendering functions.

Example local test customer: customer_id='local_test', active=true, counties=['Travis'], delivery_mode='sheets_only' or 'dry_run', spreadsheet_id from env/local config, and recipient_emails limited to the founder/operator.

title: Phase 3: build TABC scraper agent
description: Implement the script that queries TABC for chosen counties and date windows, handles pagination and source constraints, extracts all required raw fields, deduplicates obvious duplicates, and writes raw JSON artifacts for downstream processing.
design: The scraper should be boring, deterministic, and traceable. It should not clean or score leads beyond minimal parsing required to populate raw fields.
acceptance_criteria: Done when scraper can run locally for the chosen county/date range, produce raw JSON matching the contract, handle empty-result weeks, and fail loudly on site changes.
notes: Raw preservation is required so future debugging can distinguish source changes from cleaner bugs.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if the weekly run ever returns zero records, that may be legitimate. The scraper must distinguish valid empty result from site broke.

title: Implement scraper CLI inputs and run modes
description: Build a command-line interface for the scraper with inputs such as --county, --start-date, --end-date, --days, --output, and possibly --dry-run. The CLI should support the standard weekly last-seven-days run and explicit date ranges for debugging/backfills.
design: A predictable CLI makes local testing, scheduled execution, and future backfills easier. Prefer explicit dates internally even when --days is accepted as shorthand.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: scraper can be run for one county and date range; invalid inputs fail clearly; output path is configurable; logs identify query parameters.
notes: This CLI becomes the contract used by scheduler and manual operations.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: future self will need to rerun a specific week after failures. Date-range support avoids ad hoc code edits.

title: Implement TABC query execution and pagination
description: Implement the actual interaction with TABC search for county/date filters and collect all pages of matching results. Respect low-volume weekly use, conservative delays if needed, and any constraints discovered during source mapping.
design: Keep query execution isolated from parsing so site interaction and record extraction can be debugged separately. Capture enough raw response context to diagnose failures without manual reproduction.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: retrieves all pages for a test county/date range; handles no-result pages; handles pagination termination; logs page counts and record counts; avoids excessive request rates.
notes: This is a critical path implementation task.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: pagination bugs are a common source of silent missing leads. Always log expected versus collected page/record counts when possible.

title: Parse raw TABC records into canonical raw schema
description: Extract source fields from each TABC result/detail record and map them into the canonical raw schema. Preserve source strings where practical, normalize only enough to make dates and fields machine-readable, and include source_url or query provenance.
design: Parsing should tolerate optional/missing fields and record unknowns rather than crashing unnecessarily, while still failing on structural changes that make extraction unreliable.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: parsed records match field inventory; dates are machine-readable; missing optional fields are represented consistently; required-field failures are logged; sample records parse correctly.
notes: Avoid mixing data-cleaner responsibilities into this task.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: canonical raw schema is the handoff boundary. The cleaner can improve usability later without losing source fidelity.

title: Write raw JSON artifacts with metadata
description: Persist scraper output as raw JSON including run metadata: county, start_date, end_date, scraped_at, source method, record count, and possibly source query URLs. Store under a predictable path such as data/raw/week_of=YYYY-MM-DD/county=NAME.json or an equivalent artifact path.
design: Raw artifacts make the pipeline auditable and retryable. The sheet writer should never be the only place data exists.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: every scraper run writes a raw artifact; artifact includes metadata and records; empty valid runs are represented; downstream cleaner can consume the file directly.
notes: If GitHub Actions is used, decide whether artifacts are uploaded, committed nowhere, or stored externally.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: raw artifacts are the insurance policy against site changes, customer disputes, and cleaner regressions.

title: Add scraper failure modes and site-change detection
description: Add defensive checks that detect likely source-site changes, authentication/session failures, empty pages caused by errors, or parse failures. Emit clear nonzero exits when the run is not trustworthy.
design: Silent failure is worse than noisy failure because customers expect Monday delivery. Use explicit assertions around page shape, required headers, and minimum parse confidence.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: invalid page structure causes failure; valid empty result is distinguishable; logs explain failure reason; scheduled run can alert on nonzero exit.
notes: This task becomes more important before paid pilots.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the MVP credibility depends on knowing when the list is complete versus when the data source broke.

title: Phase 4: build data cleaner and lead prioritization agent
description: Transform raw TABC records into customer-friendly lead rows by normalizing names and addresses, calculating filing age, inferring concept category, selecting hot leads, and producing cleaned JSON/CSV compatible with Google Sheets.
design: The cleaner should increase usability without pretending to know more than the data supports. V1 categories and lead scores should be simple, transparent, and easy to explain to customers.
acceptance_criteria: Done when cleaned output matches sheet columns, hot leads are selected deterministically, and edge cases are covered by tests.
notes: Keep AI/enrichment out of v1 unless customer discovery proves it is required for payment.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: simple heuristics are a feature at this stage. They make buyer feedback clearer than opaque scoring.

title: Normalize business names conservatively
description: Implement clean_business_name from raw business_name by trimming whitespace, standardizing casing if appropriate, removing obvious legal suffix noise only when safe, and preserving the original source business_name separately.
design: Conservative normalization prevents accidental loss of legally meaningful names. The source name must remain visible in raw data and possibly in the sheet.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: common whitespace/casing issues are cleaned; source value is preserved; examples from sample data behave as expected; tests cover empty and unusual names.
notes: Do not overfit to one county naming patterns.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: names are how customers recognize prospects, so usability matters, but legal/source fidelity still matters.

title: Standardize address display fields
description: Create formatted_address and consistently populate address, city, state, zip, and county fields. Handle missing components gracefully and avoid geocoding in v1 unless later required.
design: Address cleaning should make rows readable in Sheets. Full address enrichment, geocoding, or parcel matching belongs in a later version.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: formatted address is readable; missing zip/city does not crash; original components are retained; tests cover complete and partial addresses.
notes: A readable address is usually enough for initial prospecting validation.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if buyers repeatedly ask for territory assignment or proximity, that is a v2 enrichment signal.

title: Infer concept category from business-name keywords
description: Implement simple keyword-based concept_category inference. Suggested categories: Bar, Restaurant, Club, Liquor Store, Hotel, Event Venue, Unknown. Example keywords: bar, saloon, tavern, pub, lounge, grill, kitchen, restaurant, taqueria, cafe, club, nightclub, liquor, spirits, wine, package, hotel, inn, suites, venue, hall, events.
design: Use transparent rules and include Unknown when no confident keyword exists. Avoid overstating classification accuracy.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: category rules are implemented; ordering/precedence is deterministic; Unknown is supported; tests cover representative keywords and ambiguous names.
notes: Buyer feedback should drive future category refinement.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: concept category helps customers scan the sheet, but v1 should not spend weeks on classification sophistication.

title: Calculate days since filing and basic lead score
description: Add days_since_filing from application_date and run date. Implement a simple lead_score that prioritizes recency and Approved status if useful, while keeping the formula explicit and easy to change.
design: The score should be a sorting aid, not a claim of predictive accuracy. For v1, simple recency/status logic is enough.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: days_since_filing is accurate for fixed run dates; invalid dates are handled; lead_score formula is documented in notes or code; tests cover boundary dates.
notes: Use timezone consistently, preferably America/Chicago for business context or UTC with clear conversion.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if customers define hot differently, replace this formula with their language rather than optimizing abstractly.

title: Select Monday hot list from cleaned records
description: Implement is_hot_lead and top-three hot list selection. Initial rule: choose the three most-recent records with status Approved. If fewer than three Approved records exist, decide whether to include fewer or fall back to most recent non-Approved records and document the behavior.
design: Hot list logic exists to make the email immediately useful. It should be deterministic, aligned with the MVP spec, and easy to override if buyer discovery shows that Approved is too late or Filed/Pending is more valuable for early sales outreach.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: top three Approved records are selected by recency for default v1; fewer-than-three behavior is explicit; no duplicates are selected; output can be consumed by email script; rule is documented so it can be compared against pilot feedback.
notes: Keep this simple until customers prove a better definition of hot. Watch for evidence that 'Approved' is actually a lagging signal for some ICPs.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the email teaser should create enough value to drive sheet opens and feedback.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Audit revision: watch whether Approved status is the right hot-lead signal. Some buyers may value earlier Filed/Pending applications more because they want to reach businesses before vendor decisions are made.

title: Write cleaned JSON/CSV for downstream publishing
description: Produce cleaned output from raw JSON in a stable format suitable for Google Sheets. Include the exact sheet columns, week_of, scraped_at, hot lead flags, and all v1 customer-facing fields.
design: The cleaner output is the publishing contract. Keep column names stable to avoid confusing customers week to week.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: cleaned artifact is generated; rows match expected column order; archive metadata is included; empty input produces valid empty output with headers or metadata; tests validate schema.
notes: If both JSON and CSV are produced, designate one as canonical.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: stable sheets create trust. Renaming columns should be treated as a product decision, not incidental refactoring.

title: Add data quality validation gate before publishing
description: Add a validation step between cleaning and publishing that checks required fields, date ranges, duplicate rates, suspiciously low/high record counts, allowed status values, blank hot lead inputs, and schema/column compatibility. The gate should stop customer publishing when data is untrustworthy while allowing clearly valid empty weeks.
design: This protects users from bad sheets. The worst MVP failure is not a failed run; it is a polished email linking to incorrect or stale data. Validation should produce a clear pass/fail summary for logs and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: validation runs before sheet write/email; required-field failures block publishing; valid empty results pass with explicit no-records status; duplicate counts are reported; abnormal record count warnings are visible; no secrets are logged.
notes: Start with simple deterministic checks. Advanced anomaly detection is not needed for v1.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: when a customer reports a bad lead, ask whether a data-quality gate could have caught it and add the check if practical.

title: Phase 5: publish weekly lead list to Google Sheets
description: Use the Google Sheets API to write cleaned records into a subscriber-facing spreadsheet. Overwrite the Current Week tab on each run and append records to the Archive tab for historical continuity.
design: Google Sheets is the MVP UI. It avoids building accounts, dashboards, permissions, and export tools while giving customers something familiar and immediately usable.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the sheet writer can authenticate via service account, update Current Week, append Archive, preserve headers, and produce a shareable link for email delivery.
notes: Treat sheet formatting and stability as product experience, not just integration plumbing.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the fastest path to paid learning is a spreadsheet customers can open, sort, filter, and forward.

title: Set up Google Sheets API credentials and permissions
description: Create or configure a Google Cloud project/service account, enable the Sheets API, store credentials securely, and share the target spreadsheet with the service account. Define local and scheduled-run credential handling.
design: Use service-account auth for automation. Never commit credential JSON. In GitHub Actions, store credentials as encrypted secrets, likely base64-encoded if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: service account can read/write the test spreadsheet; credentials are loaded securely; missing/invalid credentials fail clearly; setup steps are recorded in bead notes.
notes: This blocks all sheet writing tasks.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: many sheet bugs are actually permission bugs. Verify the spreadsheet is explicitly shared with the service account email.

title: Define spreadsheet tabs, columns, and formatting
description: Define the Current Week and Archive tab structure. Current Week is overwritten each run. Archive is appended each run. Columns should include Business Name, Clean Business Name, Concept Category, License Type, Status, Application Date, Days Since Filing, Address, City, County, Applicant Name, Source URL, Hot Lead, week_of, and scraped_at where appropriate.
design: Design the sheet for buyer scanning: hot leads should be obvious, source links should be available, and columns should not jump around between weeks. The sheet should answer who the business is, what happened, where it is, how recent it is, why it matters, and where the source record came from.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: column list and order are fixed; Current Week and Archive responsibilities are explicit; formatting/usability decisions are recorded; empty-week behavior is defined; columns map to ICP workflow; feedback/status placement is considered.
notes: Archive may include metadata columns that are hidden or placed at the end. The Current Week tab should feel like a product, not a database dump.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the spreadsheet is the product surface. A clean, stable schema improves perceived value without a web app.

title: Implement Current Week overwrite
description: Implement sheet writer behavior that clears or replaces the Current Week tab and writes the latest cleaned rows with headers. It should handle empty weeks gracefully and avoid leaving stale rows behind.
design: Overwriting prevents customers from confusing this week lead list with prior weeks. Clearing stale rows is essential when the new week has fewer records than the old week.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: Current Week tab reflects only the latest run; headers are present; stale rows are removed; empty weeks show a clear no-records state or headers-only state; write operation is idempotent.
notes: This task depends on sheet schema and Google auth.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: stale sheet rows can destroy trust because customers may call old leads thinking they are new.

title: Implement Archive append with deduplication guard
description: Append cleaned records to the Archive tab with week_of and scraped_at metadata. Add a deduplication guard based on a stable record key if possible, such as source record ID or a composite of business name, address, application date, license type, and county.
design: Archive supports historical review and future analytics, but should not create duplicate rows on reruns. If perfect source IDs are unavailable, use a documented best-effort composite key.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: archive append works; rerunning same input does not duplicate rows or duplicate behavior is explicitly controlled; metadata columns are populated; row count is logged.
notes: Archive is useful for churn prevention and future product insight.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: customers may later ask for trends, and archive data gives the founder leverage without introducing a database yet.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Audit revision: archive append and dedupe should be P0 because reruns are inevitable and duplicate archive rows can break customer trust quickly.

title: Generate or store subscriber sheet link
description: Ensure the pipeline has the correct Google Sheet URL to include in delivery emails. For v1 this may be a single shared pilot spreadsheet or manually cloned sheets per customer.
design: Do not build a multi-tenant permission system yet. Choose the simplest sharing model compatible with pilot privacy expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: email script can access the correct sheet link; sharing settings are understood; pilot-specific sheet strategy is recorded; no accidental public exposure occurs.
notes: If multiple customers require separate sheets, manage via config rather than SaaS accounts.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: one shared sheet is simplest but may expose customer activity or customization limits. Reassess when pilots are real.

title: Improve customer-facing sheet usability and actionability
description: Define and implement lightweight usability improvements for the Google Sheet so users can act without explanation: frozen header row, filters enabled, clear sorting by hot lead/recency, readable date formats, optional conditional highlighting for Hot Lead and Approved status, source links, and a short last-updated/run-summary area if feasible.
design: The spreadsheet is the MVP product UI. Small formatting choices can materially improve perceived quality and reduce support questions without requiring a web app.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: sheet is scannable on first open; headers are frozen; filters/sorting are usable; hot leads stand out; dates and addresses are readable; source URLs are accessible; empty weeks are clearly communicated.
notes: Keep formatting automated and minimal. Do not spend time on pixel-perfect design.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: user value is not just data availability; it is speed from email open to sales action.

title: Phase 6: deliver Monday email notification
description: Send a Monday morning email telling subscribers the weekly TABC list is ready, linking to the Google Sheet, and summarizing the top hot leads. This turns the sheet into a delivered product rather than a passive artifact.
design: Use the simplest reliable email mechanism first: Zapier, Google Apps Script, Gmail API, Postmark, SendGrid, or another provider. The key is timely delivery and easy debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the email can be sent automatically with sheet link and hot lead summary, and failure is visible to the operator.
notes: Email open/reply behavior is an early customer engagement signal.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: delivery cadence creates product habit. Monday 9am matters because customers should start the week with leads ready.

title: Choose email delivery mechanism
description: Decide whether v1 email should use Zapier/Gmail scheduled send, Google Apps Script, Gmail API, SendGrid, Postmark, or another provider. Base the decision on setup speed, deliverability, cost, automation support, and ease of including dynamic hot leads.
design: Manual/low-code is acceptable for MVP if it reliably sends the right message. Developer-controlled email becomes more attractive when personalization or logging matters.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: provider/mechanism chosen; required credentials/config are known; sending limits are acceptable; fallback/manual send procedure is recorded.
notes: Do not let email-provider choice delay data validation.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: deliverability matters once pilots pay, but the first version can be simpler if it proves the habit.

title: Create delivery email template and hot-list summary
description: Create the Monday delivery email content. Include a clear subject, sheet link, top three hot leads, county/date range, and a short call for feedback during pilots. Keep the tone useful and concise.
design: The email should answer: what is ready, where do I click, which leads should I look at first, what date/county window was covered, and how can I quickly send feedback? Avoid marketing fluff.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: subject and body template exist; dynamic values are defined; top hot leads render correctly; run window is included; empty-hot-list behavior is defined; pilot feedback prompt is included; reply-to/contact path is clear.
notes: Suggested subject: Your Weekly TABC Hot List is Ready. Email is both delivery mechanism and learning loop.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the email is part of the product experience and a feedback collection mechanism, not just a notification.

title: Implement or configure automated email send
description: Implement the selected email send mechanism so the weekly run can send the template with the correct sheet link and hot lead rows. Include dry-run/test-recipient support to avoid accidentally emailing customers during development.
design: Separate test sends from production sends. Make recipients configurable and log enough details to confirm delivery attempts without exposing secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: test email sends successfully; production recipient config is supported; sheet link and hot leads are inserted; failures produce visible errors; dry-run mode is available or equivalent.
notes: This task depends on hot lead selection and sheet link availability.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: never test email automation directly on all customers. Use a founder/test recipient first.

title: Phase 7: schedule, deploy, and operate the weekly run
description: Deploy the pipeline so it runs automatically before Monday morning delivery. Recommended MVP deployment is GitHub Actions scheduled workflow unless Playwright/browser needs make a small VPS more practical.
design: The run should be observable and recoverable. A founder should know whether the weekly list succeeded before customers expect it.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the full pipeline runs on schedule, secrets are configured, logs/artifacts are available, and failures alert the operator.
notes: Choose deployment for reliability and simplicity, not scale.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: automation is the product promise. If the founder has to touch raw data every week, the MVP has not met its own spec.

title: Choose GitHub Actions, VPS cron, or Cloud Scheduler deployment
description: Select the production runtime. GitHub Actions is recommended for simple scheduled Python jobs. VPS cron may be better if Playwright/browser automation is required. Google Cloud Run plus Cloud Scheduler is more scalable but probably overkill for v1.
design: Base the decision on scraper stack, secret handling, run duration, dependency complexity, logs, and cost. Avoid infrastructure that slows customer validation.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: deployment target chosen; rationale recorded; schedule timezone is defined; operational owner knows where logs and secrets live.
notes: If in doubt and Requests works, use GitHub Actions.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: infrastructure can be migrated later. Do not optimize prematurely for scale before paid pilots.

title: Implement end-to-end pipeline command
description: Create a single pipeline entry point that runs scrape, clean, sheet write, and email steps in order, while still allowing each stage to be run independently. The command should accept config for county/date range and test versus production mode.
design: An end-to-end command reduces scheduler complexity and makes local rehearsal straightforward. Stage boundaries should remain visible in logs, and publishing/email should be gated on validation so bad data does not reach users.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: one command can run the full weekly workflow; each stage logs start/end counts; validation gate runs before publishing; failures stop downstream unsafe actions; test mode can avoid customer email; customer config can drive multiple pilot deliveries.
notes: This task depends on the core scraper, cleaner, sheet writer, email components, data-quality gate, and customer delivery config.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the founder should be able to run the Monday job manually if the scheduler fails, without editing code.

title: Configure weekly schedule for Monday delivery
description: Configure the selected scheduler to run the pipeline early enough that the sheet is ready before Monday 9am Central time. If using GitHub Actions, account for UTC cron and daylight savings considerations.
design: The schedule should allow time for retries before the customer-facing email. Consider running data refresh Sunday night or early Monday and sending email at 9am Central.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: schedule is configured; timezone conversion is documented; test manual trigger exists; run completes before delivery window; secrets are available in runtime.
notes: GitHub Actions cron uses UTC, so Texas timing must be explicitly considered.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: schedule drift and daylight savings can cause surprising delivery times. Verify the first few runs manually.

title: Add logging, run summary, and failure alerts
description: Add clear logs and run summary output: counties processed, date range, raw record count, cleaned record count, sheet rows written, archive rows appended, hot leads selected, email send status, and failure reason if any. Add an operator alert path for failed scheduled runs.
design: The founder needs a fast answer to did Monday delivery work? Logs should be concise but complete enough to diagnose common issues.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: every run produces a summary; nonzero failures are visible; operator receives or can inspect alerts; no secrets are logged; empty valid weeks are distinguishable from failures.
notes: For GitHub Actions, native failure emails may be enough initially, but explicit summaries are still valuable.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: reliable operations are part of the MVP value proposition even before the product has a UI.

title: Create operator run summary and optional customer-facing status
description: Create a concise run summary that can be used by the operator and optionally shown in the sheet/email: run timestamp, date window, counties processed, raw count, cleaned count, published count, archive count, hot lead count, validation status, and any warnings.
design: Run transparency helps the founder trust the automation and helps customers understand whether a no-leads week is legitimate. It also shortens debugging when something goes wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: run summary is generated every run; summary is included in logs; warnings are visible; optional customer-facing summary does not expose internals or secrets; no-record weeks are clearly labeled.
notes: This complements logging but frames the output as product/operations information rather than raw logs.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if customers ask whether the list is complete, a clear run window and county summary answers that before support is needed.

title: Define manual fallback delivery path for critical weekly failures
description: Define what the founder does if automation fails close to Monday delivery: manually collect data if possible, publish a partial/no-data notice, delay email, or send a transparent issue note. Include decision criteria for when to send, delay, or skip customer delivery.
design: A small paid pilot can tolerate occasional transparency, but not silence. A fallback plan protects trust without over-engineering high availability.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: fallback decision tree is recorded; customer communication language is drafted in bead notes or email template; test mode/customer suppression is considered; operator knows how to recover or communicate by Monday morning.
notes: This is especially important before first paid customer delivery.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: v1 systems fail. Trust is preserved by honest, timely communication more than by pretending the system is perfect.

title: Phase 8: test and verify the MVP pipeline
description: Verify that the MVP works end-to-end before relying on it for customer delivery. Include unit tests for transformations, integration tests for sheet writing/email where practical, and manual dry-runs with known sample data.
design: Testing should protect the weekly delivery promise and avoid overbuilt test harnesses. Focus on schema stability, transformation correctness, idempotency, and integration credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Done when local and scheduled dry-runs pass, key tests run in CI or before deployment, and the team has confidence in Monday delivery.
notes: The user explicitly values automation with no human raw-data handling, so verification must cover the whole chain.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if something breaks in production, convert that failure into a regression test where practical.

title: Implement cleaner and schema unit tests
description: Test business-name normalization, address formatting, category inference, days_since_filing, lead scoring, hot lead selection, required columns, and cleaned output ordering using realistic fixtures.
design: Unit tests should lock down behavior that customers see in the sheet. Avoid fragile tests for inconsequential formatting unless it affects buyer usability.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: tests cover core cleaner functions; tests include edge cases; tests pass locally; schema/column order is asserted.
notes: This task depends on data contract and cleaner implementation.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: most customer-facing data errors will originate in transformation logic, so this is high-leverage testing.

title: Run integration dry-run against test spreadsheet and test email
description: Execute the full pipeline using sample or live limited data against a test Google Sheet and test email recipient. Confirm that raw output, cleaned output, sheet update, archive append, and email rendering all work together.
design: Do not send to customers until this passes. Use a separate test spreadsheet or test customer config to avoid damaging pilot data. Dry-run should evaluate user-facing quality, not just API success.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: full dry-run succeeds; Current Week contents are correct and usable; Archive behavior is correct; validation gate result is visible; email contains correct sheet link, hot leads, run window, and feedback prompt; logs/run summary match actual outputs.
notes: This is the final technical and product-experience gate before pilot delivery.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: dry-run should be repeated after credential changes, sheet schema changes, or source-site changes.

title: Document and test rerun/backfill procedure
description: Define how to rerun a failed week or backfill a historical date range without duplicating archive rows or emailing customers accidentally. This can be a bead-contained runbook rather than a separate markdown file.
design: Rerun safety is essential once customers rely on the list. The procedure should specify when to use test mode, how to verify rows, and how to resend emails if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: rerun command is known; archive duplicate behavior is understood; customer-email suppression is supported; procedure is recorded in notes/comments.
notes: This can be P2 for MVP but should be complete before broader rollout.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: failures are inevitable. A known recovery path keeps the founder from improvising under Monday pressure.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Audit revision: rerun/backfill moved from P2 to P1 because even a tiny pilot needs a clear recovery path before Monday delivery failures happen.

title: Phase 9: launch paid pilot and learning loop
description: Use the automated weekly list to sell and service a small group of pilot customers. The purpose is to validate willingness to pay, learn which fields matter, and decide whether to expand counties, enrich data, or build a SaaS interface.
design: Pilot scope should remain concierge. Manually onboard customers, manually manage payment if needed, and let feedback drive v2. Do not build billing or account systems before payment demand is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Done when 3-5 pilot customers have received live weekly lists, feedback is tracked, and a go/no-go/v2 decision is made based on payment and engagement signals.
notes: Business learning is the ultimate output of the MVP.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: if users open the sheet, ask for more counties, request specific fields, or pay to continue, that is stronger evidence than compliments.

title: Define pilot offer and pricing test
description: Define the initial commercial offer. Suggested options: 49/month for one county, 99/month for three counties, 199/month for statewide/metro bundle later, or a simple 100/month concierge pilot with cancel-anytime terms.
design: Pricing is a learning tool at this stage. The goal is not perfect packaging; it is to discover whether customers attach budget to the weekly signal.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: pilot price is chosen; included counties and delivery cadence are clear; cancellation terms are simple; what is not included is explicit.
notes: Avoid free pilots unless necessary; even a small payment creates stronger signal.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: a paid pilot validates the business model more than feature requests from non-paying prospects.

title: Onboard 3-5 pilot customers manually
description: Recruit and onboard three to five pilot customers. Collect target counties, recipient emails, sheet-sharing preferences, and feedback expectations. Keep onboarding manual to avoid premature product surface area.
design: Manual onboarding is acceptable because the MVP is validating the data product. Track what customers ask for repeatedly because those requests shape v2.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: 3-5 pilots are identified or attempted; contact and delivery preferences are captured; each pilot has access to the sheet; delivery expectations are set.
notes: This depends on at least a working internal MVP and pilot offer.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: customer-specific county demand may reveal the best expansion path better than market-size guesses.

title: Track weekly engagement, objections, and feature requests
description: After each delivery, track whether customers opened/responded, which leads they found useful, what fields they requested, whether timing worked, and whether they would pay/continue. Convert repeated needs into v2 beads only after patterns emerge.
design: Use structured notes: customer, week, sheet opened/responded if known, useful leads, contacted leads, missing data, objection, requested county/category, willingness to pay, follow-up action. Tie feedback back to predefined success thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: feedback is collected for each pilot delivery; repeated themes are summarized; v2 candidates are ranked by revenue impact; churn/non-use reasons are captured; success metrics are updated with observed evidence.
notes: The feedback loop is how this avoids becoming a feature factory. Treat feedback as data, not anecdotes.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the MVP main job is to generate market evidence. Treat feedback as data, not anecdotes.

title: Make v2/go-no-go decision after pilot period
description: After an initial pilot period, decide whether to continue, pivot, or stop. Evaluate data reliability, customer engagement, payment conversion, requested enrichment, and operational burden. If continuing, define v2 scope such as enrichment, more counties, better scoring, CRM integrations, or a dashboard.
design: Decision should be evidence-based. Avoid building v2 because the MVP is technically interesting; build v2 only if customers show payment or strong intent.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: pilot results summarized; continue/pivot/stop decision recorded; if continue, top v2 investments are selected; if stop/pivot, reasons are explicit.
notes: This is the business closure bead for MVP v1.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Future-self note: the right answer may be sell a concierge data service longer rather than build software. Let revenue guide the next step.

title: Add lightweight feedback capture to sheet and email
description: Add a low-friction way for pilot users to give feedback after each weekly delivery, such as a reply-to prompt in the email, a feedback link, or a short question in the sheet. Capture whether leads were useful, what fields were missing, whether they contacted anyone, and what county/category they want next.
design: The MVP must learn from real usage. Feedback capture should be embedded in the weekly habit rather than relying on separate long interviews.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: email or sheet includes a clear feedback mechanism; feedback questions map to v2 decisions; responses are tracked in the feedback loop bead; users are not burdened with long surveys.
notes: Keep this lightweight and founder-operated.

comments.author: abacus-ai
comments.text: Reasoning: the best product signal is what users do after receiving the list. Ask immediately while context is fresh.

title: Phase 1: Extract search form fields from TABC site
description: Extract the actual input field names and values from the TABC search forms to understand how to query for applications.

title: Bug Fix: Renamed src/logging.py → logger_utils.py
description: Fixed critical naming conflict where src/logging.py conflicted with Python standard library logging module. File renamed to logger_utils.py - no code changes needed.

title: P0: Unit Tests Without Mocks - Core Service Layer
description: Implement comprehensive unit tests for core service layer WITHOUT using mocks or fake objects. Focus on real database connections, actual API calls (with rate limiting), and realistic test data generation.

title: Phase 1: Validate TABC public data access method
description: Investigate whether TABC provides an official API or if we need to scrape specific pages. Check the license application status page and approved labels search for data structure.
